context-group.context:
#: enterprise/frontend/src/metabase-enterprise/google_drive/PausedModal.tsx:22
✨ AI Context This string is the main error message shown in a modal dialog when a Google Drive file upload to Metabase fails because the connected storage (data warehouse) is full or paused. The modal component is `PausedModal` in `enterprise/frontend/src/metabase-enterprise/google_drive/PausedModal.tsx`. It is rendered by `FileUploadErrorModal` when the backend upload error message contains code `497`, which indicates that uploads are paused due to storage limits: - `FileUploadErrorModal` inspects the upload error text (`children`). - If the database is an attached data warehouse (`isDwh`) and `isPausedError(children)` returns true (message includes `"Code: 497"`), it logs the original error to the console and instead shows `PausedModal`. Within `PausedModal`, this string appears as the bold, large title text at the top of the modal, centered above further explanatory body text and actions. It tells the user that their file could not be uploaded because the storage used for uploads is full. Immediately below this title, the body text varies depending on whether the current user is an admin: - Admins see guidance to add more storage or connect a database: `"Add more storage to your Metabase or connect a database to store the uploaded files."` - Non-admin users see: `"Please contact your admin to add more storage."` Below the text, the modal displays different buttons depending on admin status: - Admins get a primary button linking to the Metabase storage settings page (`Add more storage`) and a `Cancel` button. - Non-admins get a single `OK` button to dismiss the modal. Thus, this string is an end-user facing error title in a Google Drive upload flow, used in a blocking modal that appears when storage capacity has been exceeded. It should sound clear, urgent, but not highly technical, and it is always followed by more detailed instructions and one or more action buttons. ✨ 🔚

#: frontend/src/metabase/admin/performance/utils.tsx:148 #: frontend/src/metabase/admin/performance/utils.tsx:160 #, javascript-format
✨ AI Context This string is used in the Metabase admin performance scheduling UI when parsing cron expressions entered by the user. In `frontend/src/metabase/admin/performance/utils.tsx`, the function `cronToScheduleSettings_unmemoized` analyzes the parts of a cron expression (minute, hour, day-of-month, month, weekday) to infer a schedule. When the `weekday` portion of the cron expression is expected to start with a numeric day-of-week but does not (e.g. it cannot match `/^\d+/`), or when the part after the weekday (like the frame after `#` or `L`) is missing/invalid, the code throws an `Error` with this translated message: `t\`The cron expression contains an invalid weekday: ${weekday}\``. The `{0}` placeholder will be replaced with the offending `weekday` field from the cron expression, such as `Monn`, `8`, or another invalid token, and will appear in an error shown to the user configuring a scheduled task or alert in the admin performance section. ✨ 🔚

The number in the string is a count of selected users and must agree grammatically with the plural form of “users” in the target language. trans-unit.note:
The translation is correct, but just to clarify the following:
In Portuguese, the time of day is singular or plural depending on the number:
at 1:00pm → à 1 hora (singular)
at 2:00pm → às 2 horas (plural)
The translator found a clever workaround by using "(s)" to cover both cases, but from a UI/UX perspective, it might be worth considering separate variables for singular and plural time formats.

The placeholder `{0}` corresponds to the maximum allowed file size in megabytes (`MAX_UPLOAD_STRING`). We’ll be defaulting to “Blocked”, the least permissive View data access, to prevent any unintended access to data.
trans-unit.target: 향후 릴리스에서 데이터베이스(또는 해당 스키마 또는 테이블)에 대한 그룹의 보기 데이터 액세스가 여전히 "셀프 서비스 없음(사용 중단됨)"으로 설정되어 있는 경우, Metabase는 전체 데이터베이스에 대한 해당 그룹의 보기 데이터 액세스를 "차단됨"으로 자동 변경합니다. 데이터에 대한 의도치 않은 액세스를 방지하기 위해 뷰 데이터 액세스가 가장 적게 허용되는 "차단됨"으로 기본 설정됩니다.

✨ AI Context This text is used as the empty state helper message in the query results area for native/SQL queries. In `QueryVisualization.jsx`, it appears inside `VisualizationEmptyState`, which is shown in the main query builder when: - there is no `result.error`, - there is no `result.data`, - the query is not currently running (`!isRunning`), - and there is no "dirty state" being shown. `VisualizationEmptyState` renders an icon and instructions on how to run the query (including a keyboard shortcut), and then shows this string below those instructions. So the user sees this text in the main results pane before they have run a question, indicating where results will appear once the query is executed. In `NativeQueryModal.tsx`, the same text is used in `QueryExecutionEmptyState` for the native query editing modal. It is shown when the modal is open for a query that has not yet been executed and there is no initial data. It appears under similar "how to run your code" instructions and an icon, in the results area on the right-hand side of the modal. The text therefore always refers to the results panel where query results will be shown after executing the query. ✨ 🔚

trans-unit.resname: In a future release, if a group's View data access for a database (or any of its schemas or tables) is still set to No self-service (Deprecated), Metabase will automatically change that group's View data access for the entire database to Blocked. We'll be defaulting to Blocked, the least permissive View data access, to prevent any unintended access to data.
trans-unit.source: In a future release, if a group's View data access for a database (or any of its schemas or tables) is still set to No self-service (Deprecated), Metabase will automatically change that group's View data access for the entire database to Blocked. We'll be defaulting to Blocked, the least permissive View data access, to prevent any unintended access to data.

`{0}` will be replaced with a table name or a localized word for "record/records" depending on context. `{1}` is always an empty string and should not be surfaced to the user; it only exists to make this key unique in the translation catalog.
This title appears in the UI as the label for the drill action under the "records" section, often in a chart or dashboard when a user clicks a data point to inspect underlying records. ✨ 🔚

#: frontend/src/metabase/visualizations/visualizations/SankeyChart/chart-definition.ts:232 #, javascript-format
✨ AI Context This message appears as a validation error in the Sankey visualization settings in Metabase. When the user configures a Sankey chart and the underlying data would produce more unique nodes than the chart implementation allows, Metabase throws a `ChartSettingsError` with this string. It is shown in the UI near the visualization settings as feedback explaining why the chart cannot be rendered with the current data. The `{0}` placeholder is replaced by the constant `MAX_SANKEY_NODES`, the maximum permitted number of distinct nodes derived from the selected source and target columns. Technical details: - File: `frontend/src/metabase/visualizations/visualizations/SankeyChart/chart-definition.ts` - Logic: counts unique node values from the selected source and target columns; if `nodesCount > MAX_SANKEY_NODES`, this error is thrown. - Audience: end users configuring or viewing a Sankey chart in Metabase. - Tone: concise, explanatory limit message, not a fatal application error. ✨ 🔚

It strips the `Coercion/` prefix, splits the remaining string on `->` into a left term and right term, then calls `treatTermsAndJoin(leftTerm, rightTerm)`. In `treatTermsAndJoin`, the left and right terms are individually humanized and then joined with this localized arrow string: `[treatedLeftTerm, treatedRightTerm].join(c("arrow denoting a conversion. eg: string → date").t` → `)` So, for example, a technical coercion strategy like `Coercion/ISO8601->DateTime` will be shown in the dropdown as `ISO 8601 → Datetime`, with this arrow between the two sides. The arrow visually indicates a conversion "from" the left type/value representation "to" the right type. This appears specifically in the dropdown options of the `CoercionStrategyPicker` select component (`frontend/src/metabase/metadata/components/CoercionStrategyPicker/CoercionStrategyPicker.tsx`), which is used in the data model/metadata UI when configuring how a field should be cast. ✨ 🔚

#: metabase/cache/settings.clj:8
✨ AI Context This string is the human-readable label/description for the `enable-query-caching` setting defined in `src/metabase/cache/settings.clj`. It appears in the Metabase admin/settings UI where administrators configure query caching behavior. The setting controls whether Metabase is allowed to cache the results of "slow" queries (queries that take a long time to run). When enabled (`:type :boolean`, default `true`), Metabase may store results of such queries in its cache so that subsequent runs can be served more quickly. When disabled, Metabase will not cache query results regardless of duration. Linguistically, it is a descriptive sentence shown to admins, not end-users, explaining what turning this option on will do. It should read naturally as an option description following a checkbox or toggle labeled something like "Enable query caching" or similar. ✨ 🔚

✨ AI Context This string is used in notification emails or messages generated by the Smart Scalar visualization to describe how the current metric compares to the previous hour. It appears as part of a longer sentence like "Up 5% vs. previous hour: 100". The function `smart-scalar-comparison-statement` in `src/metabase/channel/render/body.clj` builds this text based on a time unit (minute, hour, day, etc.). When the unit is `:hour`, it formats this string with `{0}` replaced by the formatted value for the previous hour: - The previous value is taken from an insight map (`previous-value`). - It is formatted with `format-scalar-value` and passed as `value` to this string. - The string is concatenated with a "delta" phrase such as "Up {0}" or "Down {0}", resulting in a full statement like "Up 10% vs. previous hour: 123". Linguistic notes: - "vs." means "versus" and indicates a comparison. It should read naturally as "compared to the previous hour" in the target language. - `{0}` is a placeholder for the numeric value (or formatted metric) from the previous hour, not for a percentage. - The colon `:` after "hour" introduces the previous value, e.g., "vs. previous hour: 123". - This is used in a metrics/analytics context describing time-based comparisons for a single numeric metric. ✨ 🔚

#: metabase/driver/common/parameters/operators.clj:61
✨ AI Context This error message is shown when a filter or parameter in a query uses an operator type that Metabase does not recognize. The message is thrown from `metabase.driver.common.parameters.operators/verify-type-and-arity` and `metabase.query_processor.parameters.operators/verify-type-and-arity` when the operator’s arity (unary, binary, variadic) has been checked, but the operator type does not match any of the known cases. It appears in backend error responses (not directly as a visible UI label) when constructing MBQL filter clauses for parameterized queries. `{0}` is replaced with the internal operator identifier (e.g. `:number/between`, `:time-interval`, or any other operator keyword) that failed to match a supported operation. ✨ 🔚

Parameters: {0} is the name of the operator with invalid values (e.g., 'equals')
#: metabase/driver/common/parameters/operators.clj:55
✨ AI Context This error message is shown when a filter or variable operator in a query is given values in the wrong format. It is used in server-side validation of parameterized queries to ensure that operators which accept a variable number of arguments (variadic operators, such as "between", "in", etc.) receive a sequential/array-like value. The placeholder {0} is programmatically replaced with the operator's type/name (for example, "between"), so translations must keep {0} exactly as-is. #: metabase/driver/util.clj:464
✨ AI Context This error message is thrown on the backend when processing database driver connection properties that have conditional visibility rules (`visible-if`). In `src/metabase/driver/util.clj`, the function `resolve-transitive-visible-if` walks the dependency graph between connection properties (e.g., host, port, SSL options) to compute transitive `visible-if` relationships. If it detects a cycle in these dependencies, it throws an exception with this message. The placeholder parameters are populated as follows: - `{0}` is the driver identifier/name (e.g., `postgres`, `mysql`). It comes from the `driver` argument passed into `resolve-transitive-visible-if`. - `{1}` is the set of property names that participate in the cycle. It is derived from `cyclic-props`, the intersection of the currently visited properties and newly discovered `visible-if` dependencies. This string is not shown directly in the UI under normal circumstances; it surfaces in logs or error responses when there is a misconfiguration or bug in a driver’s connection property metadata, specifically in their `:visible-if` definitions. ✨ 🔚

#: metabase/parameters/shared.cljc:164
✨ AI Context This string is used to format a list of 3 or more parameter values into a human‑readable phrase in filters/parameters. It appears in `src/metabase/parameters/shared.cljc` inside the `formatted-list` function: ```clojure (defn formatted-list "Given a seq of parameter values, returns them as a single comma-separated string. Does not do additional formatting on the values. The conjunction parameter determines whether to use 'and' or 'or' to join the last two items." [values & {:keys [conjunction] :or {conjunction (trs "and")}}] (condp = (count values) 1 (str (first values)) 2 (trs "{0} {1} {2}" (first values) conjunction (second values)) (trs "{0}, {1}, {2} {3}" (str/join ", " (drop-last 2 values)) (nth values (- (count values) 2)) conjunction (last values)))) ``` For 3 or more values, the final string is: - `{0}`: all but the last two values, joined by a comma and space (e.g. "A, B, C") - `{1}`: the next-to-last value - `{2}`: the conjunction word, usually localized "and" or "or" - `{3}`: the last value in the list Example with conjunction = "and": - Input values: `["A" "B" "C" "D"]` - Output: `"A, B, C and D"` This is used anywhere Metabase needs to display a list of parameter values (e.g., filter chips or parameter summaries) as a grammatically correct, localized list. ✨ 🔚

In the Metabase permissions system, revisions are append‑only audit records that track each change to permissions. trans-unit.note: Please explain what 'left join' means in this context @nazaret.lazaro @brunobergher

@mbnick1 Left joins (or joins in general) are a common operation in database querying, where data form one table is merged with another's, based on criteria.
I don't think "joins" (which include just join, but also left join, full join, outer join, etc) should ever be translated and are almost always expressed in ALL CAPS.
Also worth saying it's not a matter of compatibility, but support (the database to which the driver connects may support joins, but our driver may not for some reason).
So in this case "O driver {0} não suporta LEFT JOINs" would be the correct translation (the original string should be changed to be all caps).

#: metabase/query_processor/pipeline.clj:60 #: metabase/query_processor/postprocess.clj:62
✨ AI Context This error message is shown when Metabase fails to construct the query results reducing function (RFF) before actually reducing the result rows. It appears in two closely related situations in the query processor: - In `src/metabase/query_processor/postprocess.clj` inside `post-processing-rff`, when post-processing middleware fails to transform an existing reducing function into a new one: - The code attempts to `reduce` a list of post‑processing middleware functions over an existing RFF. - If any middleware throws an exception while building the new reducing function, Metabase catches the `Throwable` and throws an `ex-info` with this message. - The placeholder `{0}` is filled with the underlying exception message (`(ex-message e)`). - In `src/metabase/query_processor/pipeline.clj` inside the dynamic function `*reduce*`, when the initial RFF cannot be built from query metadata: - The code calls `(rff metadata)` to create the reducing function. - If this throws, Metabase wraps the error in `ex-info` with this message. In the UI this surfaces as a query error when preparing the function that will aggregate/transform query results fails, before row reduction starts. `{0}` is the human‑readable error message from the original exception, giving more detail about what went wrong when building the reducing function. ✨ 🔚

#: metabase/query_processor/setup.clj:29
✨ AI Context This error message is shown when the Metabase query processor receives a query map that does not specify a valid query type. In `src/metabase/query_processor/setup.clj`, the `query-type` function tries to determine the query type by looking up either the `:lib/type` or `:type` key in the incoming `query` map and converting it to a keyword. If neither key exists or the value is invalid, the code throws an exception with this message: `(throw (ex-info (i18n/tru "Invalid query: missing or invalid query type (:lib/type or :type)") {:query query, :type qp.error-type/invalid-query}))` This means translators should understand this is a backend validation error that will typically surface in logs, API responses, or possibly as a displayed error when a client sends a malformed or incomplete query definition to the Metabase server. It refers specifically to missing or incorrect values for the `:lib/type` or `:type` fields of an internal query object, not to end-user input fields in the UI. ✨ 🔚

#: metabase/query_processor/store.clj:135
✨ AI Context This string is used as the message of an exception thrown by the backend query processor when validating an existing metadata provider. In `src/metabase/query_processor/store.clj`, function `validate-existing-provider` checks whether a new `Database` ID being used to initialize the metadata provider matches the `Database` ID of the already-initialized provider. If they differ, it throws an `ex-info` with this text and error type `qp.error-type/invalid-query`. The message helps explain to the user (or developer) why their query is invalid: a single query is trying to involve more than one `Database`. The placeholders are filled as follows: - {0}: the ID (stringified using `pr-str`) of the new `Database` being used to initialize the metadata provider (`new-database-id`). - {1}: the ID (stringified using `pr-str`) of the already-referenced `Database` from the existing metadata provider (`existing-database-id`). This error will typically surface in logs or error dialogs when Metabase code attempts to bind a query to a different database than the one already associated with the current metadata provider context. ✨ 🔚

It appears when building SQL for a query join condition in Metabase. The message is shown when a JOIN condition incorrectly uses a field reference that should point to a column from an earlier part of the query (outside the current join), but due to fuzzy matching / malformed field reference resolution it instead resolves to a column from the current join. #: metabase/request/settings.clj:18
✨ AI Context This string is the description of an internal boolean setting named `not-behind-proxy` in `src/metabase/request/settings.clj`. The setting controls whether Metabase should treat itself as **not** running behind an HTTP proxy that provides the client IP via the `source-address-header` (by default `X-Forwarded-For`). When `not-behind-proxy` is false (the default), Metabase will look at the configured `source-address-header` to determine the real client IP instead of using the direct remote address from the TCP connection. This text appears in admin/settings and documentation to explain that this flag is about proxy/network topology and how Metabase derives the source IP for incoming HTTP requests. ✨ 🔚

#: metabase/warehouse_schema/models/field.clj:53
✨ AI Context This error message is constructed and thrown in `src/metabase/warehouse_schema/models/field.clj` inside the private function `hierarchy-keyword-in`. That function validates values for various Field model keyword columns (`:base_type`, `:effective_type`, `:semantic_type`, `:coercion_strategy`). When Metabase reads data for a Field column that is expected to be a keyword belonging to a specific type hierarchy, it calls `hierarchy-keyword-in` with: - `column-name` = the name of the Field column being validated (e.g. `:base_type`, `:effective_type`, etc.). This becomes `{0}` in the message. - `ancestor-types` = a list of allowed supertypes in the keyword hierarchy (e.g. `[:type/*]`, `[:Semantic/* :Relation/*]`). This becomes `{2}`. At runtime, the function receives a value `k` for that column, coerces it to a keyword, and checks whether it `isa?` any of the allowed ancestor types. If not, it builds this localized message with `tru` and throws an `ex-info` exception with: - `{1}` = the invalid value (printed with `pr-str`), - a 400 HTTP `:status-code`, - an `:errors` map associating the specific `column-name` to this error message, - the invalid `:value` and the allowed `:allowed-ancestors` in the exception data. So translators should keep in mind: - This string appears in API error responses when invalid Field metadata is provided (e.g., via sync, API calls, or schema definitions), not directly in the end‑user UI. - `{0}`, `{1}`, and `{2}` are developer‑oriented debug values, shown as code-like printed values (e.g. `:semantic_type`, `:type/Unknown`, `[:Semantic/* :Relation/*]`). - The tone should be precise and technical, clearly explaining that the provided value is not within the allowed type hierarchy. ✨ 🔚

#: metabase_enterprise/audit_app/permissions.clj:47 #: metabase_enterprise/audit_app/permissions.clj:51
✨ AI Context This error message is thrown when a user attempts to run a native (SQL or driver-specific) query against Metabase's internal audit database. The `check-audit-db-permissions` function in `metabase_enterprise/audit_app/permissions.clj` enforces several rules for queries on the audit DB: the user must have access to the analytics collection, only non-native queries are allowed, and only specific audit views (with names like `v_audit_log`, `v_users`, etc.) may be queried. If the query type is `:native` or the query metadata indicates it is native, Metabase throws an exception with this message and includes the query as context. This is a backend validation error, not a visible UI label, and it will typically surface to the user as an error response when they try to run a disallowed native query on the audit database. ✨ 🔚
Marcelo

context-group.context:
#: metabase_enterprise/metabot_v3/tools/filters.clj:84
✨ AI Context In `enterprise/backend/src/metabase_enterprise/metabot_v3/tools/filters.clj`, this string is used in an exception thrown when Metabot (the AI assistant) tries to apply a segment-based filter to a query but cannot find the referenced segment. The relevant code: - A filter object (`llm-filter`) may contain a `:segment-id`. - The code attempts to load the segment via `lib.metadata/segment query segment-id`. - If that call returns `nil` (segment does not exist or is not visible), it throws an exception with this message: `"Segment with id {0} not found"`. - The exception data includes `{:agent-error? true :status-code 404 :segment-id segment-id}` to signal a user-facing 404-style error from the Metabot agent. **How it appears in the UI / when it’s shown:** This message is surfaced to users interacting with Metabot when they ask a question whose generated query references a saved segment that no longer exists or is inaccessible. The `{0}` placeholder is replaced with the numeric segment ID. **Notes for translators / linguists:** - "Segment" refers to a saved filter or subset of data (a Metabase segment object), not a generic part/section of text. - `{0}` is a placeholder for a numeric database object ID and must remain in the translation. - The tone is an error message explaining that a requested saved segment cannot be found (HTTP 404-like situation). ✨ 🔚

trans-unit.target: ID가 {0} 인 측정값을 찾을 수 없습니다.

#: metabase_enterprise/remote_sync/settings.clj:24
✨ AI Context This string is the label/description for the `remote-sync-branch` admin setting in `metabase-enterprise.remote-sync.settings`. It appears in the Metabase Enterprise admin UI where an administrator configures Git-based "remote sync" of Metabase content. The setting expects the name of a Git branch (like `main`) from a remote repository specified by `remote-sync-url`. This branch is used as the one Metabase syncs with when importing/exporting content via Git. Translators should preserve the Git terminology ("remote", "branch", example `main`) and make clear that it is the name of a Git branch, not a generic description. ✨ 🔚

That setting defines a sensitive, non-exportable string value used as an HTTP Authorization Bearer token to authenticate access to a remote Git repository for Metabase's "remote sync" feature. It appears in the admin settings UI where administrators configure Git synchronization (alongside settings for branch, URL, sync type, etc.), describing what value should be entered into the `remote-sync-token` field. ✨ 🔚

#: metabase_enterprise/remote_sync/settings.clj:133
✨ AI Context This string is the description for the `remote-sync-transforms` admin setting in `metabase_enterprise/remote_sync/settings.clj`. This setting is a boolean toggle, visible only to admins, that controls whether data model transforms in Metabase are synchronized through the remote sync (Git-based) mechanism. When enabled, all transforms, their tags, and related transform jobs are treated as a single unit during remote sync operations: they are either all successfully synced together or none are, ensuring consistency. The text appears in the admin settings UI and possibly in environment variable documentation to explain this behavior to administrators configuring remote sync. ✨ 🔚

The value is an integer representing the cache time-to-live (TTL) in seconds for the "check for remote changes" operation, with a default of 60 seconds. ✨ 🔚

#: metabase_enterprise/remote_sync/settings.clj:51
✨ AI Context This string is the label/description for the `remote-sync-type` application setting that controls how Git-based remote synchronization works. It appears in the Metabase Enterprise admin settings UI for configuring Git sync. The setting is of keyword type and only accepts two values: `:read-only` (default) or `:read-write`. The text explains to admins that they must choose between these two modes, where `:read-only` means Metabase will only import from the Git repository, and `:read-write` allows two-way synchronization. ✨ 🔚

trans-unit.resname: Whether to automatically import from the remote git repository. Only applies if remote-sync-type is :read-only.

#: metabase_enterprise/remote_sync/settings.clj:68
✨ AI Context This string is the description for the `remote-sync-auto-import` application setting defined in `enterprise/backend/src/metabase_enterprise/remote_sync/settings.clj`. That setting controls whether Metabase should automatically import content from a configured remote Git repository when remote sync is enabled. It is shown wherever settings metadata is surfaced (e.g., in the Metabase admin UI, API, or documentation) to explain what this specific toggle does. It only has an effect when the related setting `remote-sync-type` is set to `:read-only`, meaning the local Metabase instance is a read-only mirror of the Git repo. If `remote-sync-type` is `:read-write`, this auto-import option is ignored. ✨ 🔚

#: metabase_enterprise/sso/api/oidc.clj:89 #: metabase_enterprise/sso/api/oidc.clj:96 #: metabase_enterprise/sso/api/oidc.clj:107 #: metabase_enterprise/sso/api/oidc.clj:125 #: metabase_enterprise/sso/api/oidc.clj:169 #: metabase_enterprise/sso/api/oidc.clj:185 #: metabase_enterprise/sso/integrations/oidc.clj:38 #: metabase_enterprise/sso/integrations/oidc.clj:72
✨ AI Context This string appears in the context of configuring and handling OpenID Connect (OIDC) based single sign-on in Metabase. It is used in backend Clojure namespaces like `metabase.sso.oidc.common`, `metabase.sso.oidc.state`, and `metabase.sso.providers.oidc` that implement "OIDC authentication" functionality.
"OIDC authentication" refers specifically to the authentication mechanism where users log in to Metabase via an external OpenID Connect identity provider (IdP). The surrounding code includes: - Common utilities for OIDC authentication (`src/metabase/sso/oidc/common.clj`). - Encrypted cookie-based state management for OIDC authentication flows and validation of post-login redirect URLs (`src/metabase/sso/oidc/state.clj`). - A base OIDC authentication provider that defines the generic OIDC auth flow that concrete providers extend (`src/metabase/sso/providers/oidc.clj`).
In the UI and error messages, this phrase is used to describe the OIDC SSO login method (e.g., in configuration screens, error messages like missing encryption key, or HTTP method not supported for starting an OIDC login). So this text appears as a backend error message in the API (and in tests) when a user tries to add a transform that is based on another question into a workspace, which is not allowed. It describes a restriction: transforms that *reference saved questions/cards* cannot be added to workspaces. ✨ 🔚
